what: ASIC ports sampled at 200 Hz from inside the modem across an off-hook seizure. Phone line unplugged, so ATD closes a relay and dials nothing.

transients: 0x1c FD->FF for a single tick (5 ms) at t=975 ms
0x1c FD->FC for two ticks (10 ms) at t=2125 ms - bit 0
all six ports read 00 for a single tick at t=2715 ms
sustained ~215 ms state at the end of the ring: 0x40 and 0x42 both FF, 0x18 FD, 0x1c 55, 0x1e 00

the_discrepancy.claim: The monitor's port-read selector and the CPU's own IN do not agree on port 0x40.
the_discrepancy.evidence: ATGLK2I0040 reports 00 in artifacts/asic-ports-01; an in al,0x40 executed on the 80186 reads 55, steadily, for 639 of 682 ticks.
the_discrepancy.status: unexplained; it means the ATGLK2I sweep is not a faithful picture of what the CPU sees

limits: The 215 ms end-of-ring state coincides with the dial abort and hangup. Attributing it to a DSP re-download is a hypothesis, not established - nothing here identifies what drove those ports.
Single-tick events are at the sampling resolution, so a 5 ms transient is indistinguishable from anything shorter that happened to be caught.
The six ports are not sampled simultaneously; they are five instructions apart within one tick.
Sampling 0x1c and 0x1e races the supervisor for mailbox status.
